content.text:
Perfect! All tests are now passing. Here's what I fixed:

## Issue 1: Governance module missing exports
The test tried to import `APPROVAL_STATUSES` directly from `governance/index.js`, but the constants were only imported internally and not re-exported. I added named exports for all the schema constants (`APPROVAL_STATUSES`, `DATA_SENSITIVITY_LEVELS`, etc.) at the top of the file.

## Issue 2: Toxicity metric receiving wrong arguments
The `toxicityMetric` function was being called with `(outputs, references)` from `runEvaluations`, but its second parameter expects `bannedTerms`. This caused the references array to be treated as banned terms, producing an incorrect score of 0 instead of 1. I wrapped the metric in an object with an `evaluate` method that only passes the outputs, so it uses the default banned terms correctly.

All 28 tests now pass across 8 test files. The fixes maintain backward compatibility and keep all existing public exports working.

result:
Perfect! All tests are now passing. Here's what I fixed:

## Issue 1: Governance module missing exports
The test tried to import `APPROVAL_STATUSES` directly from `governance/index.js`, but the constants were only imported internally and not re-exported. I added named exports for all the schema constants (`APPROVAL_STATUSES`, `DATA_SENSITIVITY_LEVELS`, etc.) at the top of the file.

## Issue 2: Toxicity metric receiving wrong arguments
The `toxicityMetric` function was being called with `(outputs, references)` from `runEvaluations`, but its second parameter expects `bannedTerms`. This caused the references array to be treated as banned terms, producing an incorrect score of 0 instead of 1. I wrapped the metric in an object with an `evaluate` method that only passes the outputs, so it uses the default banned terms correctly.

All 28 tests now pass across 8 test files. The fixes maintain backward compatibility and keep all existing public exports working.
